title: Loss Limiting and Anti-Fixation Mechanisms
description: Three-layer loop detection + forced redirection + call-signature deduplication
detail:
CHYing ABANDON mechanism:
1. Detect looping: failure keywords / tool-call signatures (remove IPs and keep only paths to avoid false positives) / block after 3 attempts on the same CVE
2. When triggered, force a change of direction (hook interception)
3. Thresholds are hard to tune: too low kills reasonable exploration, too high wastes time
Supporting practices (harness engineering consensus): prevent fixation on a single tool, use step thresholds and multi-level queue rescheduling, degrade on stalls and inject hints, and have an observer periodically read progress to detect drift.
Sapper's corresponding approach: write timeboxes into intent docs; automatically write hints on verify failures; stop if the commander reasons `noop` twice in a row; sweep/command retargeting is itself a form of loss limiting.
Source: CHYing-agent + l3yx harness documentation
